items.question: How is the supreme principle Shiva conceived at the highest limit?
premises: At the end of all levels stands a supreme principle.
This principle is beyond all coverings, all-pervading, independent, and all-knowing.
This conceived principle is identified as Shiva.
items.inference: Even the highest conceptualized Shiva is imagined as a supreme, free, omniscient, all-pervading reality beyond all coverings.
uncertainties: yāvadante could be read as 'at the end of everything' or more specifically 'at the end of the sequence of principles'.
items.plain_english: At the final limit, one conceives a supreme principle beyond all coverings, all-pervading, independent, all-knowing, and called Shiva.

items.question: What happens when even the conceived Shiva is seen in unconstructed awareness?
premises: Even the conceived Shiva appears reflected in the mirror of unconstructed noble awareness.
One can see this while free from conceptualization.
Such seeing leads to becoming Bhairava.
items.inference: When the highest conceived Shiva is recognized as a reflection in nonconceptual awareness, the seer spontaneously becomes Bhairava.
uncertainties: The compound tadapyakalpitodārasaṃviddarpaṇabimbitam can be parsed in slightly different ways, but the overall sense is clear.
items.plain_english: Seeing even that conceived Shiva reflected in the mirror of unconstructed, noble awareness, and free from conceptual thought, one becomes Bhairava oneself.

items.question: What analogy illustrates stable nonconceptual awareness of a single object?
premises: One may see a red object in front through nonconceptual awareness.
Through its various channels, awareness can settle on one partless object.
This settling is firm and undivided.
items.inference: Nonconceptual awareness can apprehend a single object as an undivided whole despite multiple avenues of perception.
uncertainties: tattaddvāraniraṃśaikaghaṭasaṃvitti is a dense compound; 'channels' is an interpretive gloss for dvāra.
items.plain_english: Just as one who sees a red object in front with nonconceptual awareness becomes firmly established in the undivided awareness of that one pot through its various channels.

rows.grounds: extends the analogy to all aggregates

items.question: How does recognition operate across all aggregates from earth onward?
premises: The analogy extends from a single object to every aggregate beginning with earth.
One can recognize one's own self in relation to these aggregates.
The self then shines forth as full.
items.inference: By recognizing the self through every aggregate, one experiences the self as inherently full.
items.plain_english: In the same way, recognizing one's own self through each and every aggregate beginning with earth, one shines forth as truly full.

items.question: What three contemplations constitute the Shambhava means?
premises: One may contemplate that this arises from me.
One may contemplate that this is reflected in me alone.
One may contemplate that this is not different from me.
items.inference: The Shambhava means is articulated as a threefold contemplative recognition of source, reflection, and non-difference.
items.plain_english: This has arisen from me, this is reflected in me alone, and this is not different from me: in this threefold way is the Shambhava means.

rows.grounds: states that the summary is given

items.question: How does the threefold formula relate to creation, maintenance, and withdrawal?
premises: The threefold formula summarizes creation, maintenance, and withdrawal.
This summary is presented as an established teaching.
The Spanda teaching is cited as its source.
items.inference: The Shambhava threefold recognition corresponds to the cosmic functions of creation, maintenance, and withdrawal and is grounded in the Spanda teaching.
uncertainties: The fragment yatra sthitaṃ yataśceti is compressed; the exact syntactic link to the citation is slightly elliptical.
items.plain_english: This is the summary of creation, maintenance, and withdrawal. As it is established and taught, the Spanda teaching states it.

items.question: What more needs to be said once awareness is known as sovereign and universal?
premises: By this alone the supreme sovereign nature of awareness is made known.
Its being the self of all is also made known.
No further defining mark is required.
items.inference: Once awareness is recognized as sovereign and the self of all, no additional characteristic is needed to define it.
items.plain_english: By this alone the supreme sovereign nature of awareness and its identity as the self of all are made known; what other defining mark need be stated?

items.question: How does recognizing oneself as creator reveal Bhairava identity?
premises: The universe is manifested in one's own self, the space of consciousness.
One recognizes oneself as the creator whose self is the universe.
This expansive recognition is Bhairava identity.
items.inference: Recognizing oneself as the universal creator within consciousness itself is the unfolding of Bhairava identity.
items.plain_english: In my own self, in the space of consciousness, I manifest the universe; through this expansive recognition as the creator whose self is the universe, Bhairava identity unfolds.

items.question: How does recognizing maintenance in oneself reveal universal form?
premises: The entire group of six paths is reflected in oneself alone.
One recognizes oneself as the maker of maintenance.
This recognition becomes a clear universal identity.
items.inference: Seeing all manifestation reflected in oneself as its sustainer reveals one's universal form.
uncertainties: ṣaḍadhva refers to the sixfold path system; rendered plainly as 'group of six paths'.
items.plain_english: The entire group of the six paths is reflected in me alone; recognizing 'I am the maker of maintenance' is this clear universal form.

items.question: What brings the universe to melt and the seer to become still?
premises: The self is described as matted with flames of ever-risen great awakening.
The universe melts in that self.
Seeing this dissolution in oneself brings stillness.
items.inference: Recognizing the universe dissolving in the blazing awakened self leads to profound stillness.
uncertainties: jaṭilatā evokes Shiva's matted hair; the gloss keeps the image but remains interpretive.
items.plain_english: Seeing that this universe melts in me, in the self matted with the flames of ever-risen great awakening, one becomes still.

items.question: How is the self recognized as the fire that burns the dream of samsara?
premises: Samsara is described as a dream-house filled with endless varied beings.
The self is recognized as Shiva, the burner of that dream-house.
This recognition exults as a consuming fire.
items.inference: Recognizing oneself as Shiva is to know oneself as the fire that consumes the dream-like world of samsara.
items.plain_english: I am Shiva, the exulting fire that burns the dream-house of samsara, filled with endless varied beings.

items.question: What realization of creation, maintenance, and dissolution reveals the fourth state?
premises: The whole world arises from the self in manifold difference.
When dissolved in the self, no separate other remains.
One may see creation, maintenance, and dissolution as play within a partless reality.
items.inference: Seeing the world's arising and dissolution as play in the partless self reveals the fourth state.
uncertainties: padabhitaḥ is slightly unusual; taken here as 'from the standpoint of the state/pada'.
items.plain_english: The whole world arises from me in many differentiated forms, yet when it dissolves in me no other remains. One who sees creation, maintenance, and dissolution as play in a partless reality shines forth in the fourth state.
